To be completely pedantic, the sword shown isn't a Viking Era sword at all. The crossguard is too wide, and the brazil nut pomel wasn't in use during that period.

It's definitely a Carolingian or pre-knightly arming sword. I preserved it from the original article.

A "true" viking sword, is most typified by the very famous "ulfbhert" swords (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ulfberht_swords).

Basically no crossguard, the knurled "knuckle" pomels, and double edged with no taper would typify a viking age sword.

Protip: Always google something you're unfamiliar or unsure about.

An Arming Sword is the technical name of what most people nowadays would call a longsword. One handed, simple crossguard, blade between 28-31 inches (70-80 cm). They are also known as Knightly Swords.

To be fair, though, the sword in question would likely be simply called a "Viking Age Sword" or Carolingian Sword.

Nevermind. It's dated to a transitional period between Carolingian and Knightly Swords, where neither terms would be a perfect fit.
